domain: 18th-19th-century inland-navigation lock-keeping and summit-level canal water management (pound-lock hydraulics, reservoir economy)
axioms: The summit reservoir is finite: every lockage spends water that cannot be recovered until the next feed, so throughput is bounded by a scarce shared resource that must be metered against its actual current level, not a nominal capacity.

Isolation is a build-time chamber-sizing choice: a lock is cut wide (broad) or narrow before any vessel arrives; two vessels share a chamber only if it was deliberately constructed to hold them, so the isolation granularity of parallel work is largely a structural property of the work, not a free runtime dial.

Priming a lock costs water: opening and filling a chamber to pass a vessel has a fixed cost, so a regulation check or setup step is only worth running when the passage it guards is worth more than its priming.
A staircase lock couples passages a flight keeps independent: when chambers share an intermediate gate, one vessel's exit is the next's entrance, silently serializing what looked parallel.
A dry lockage wastes the whole fill: cycling a chamber for a vessel that never comes spends water for nothing, so building capacity ahead of demonstrated traffic is a loss until traffic is measured.

Drought discipline forbids starting a flight you cannot finish: a vessel stranded between chambers on an empty summit blocks the entire canal, so each stage of passage must be able to hold a vessel at rest.
primitives: reservoir level (real remaining token / rate budget)
lockage (a single fan-out of width N)
chamber and its width (isolation domain: per-repo worktree vs interlock-shared tree)
water spent per lockage (token multiplier, wall-time, rate consumption)
priming cost (pre-spawn intermap change_impact + interlock dry-run; ~200-500ms+disk worktree setup)
gate-and-paddle ordering (sequence of pre-dispatch checks before the top gate opens)
flight vs staircase (independent per-nested-repo passages vs shared intermediate gate: main-checkout Dolt redirect, root worktree, root-spanning publish waves)
dry lockage (dead-code-until-proven controller capacity built ahead of measured conflict)
failure_mode: Blind to ledger/ownership double-counting: it will not notice that a capability is posted to two orchestrators (Rimsky and Mycroft) or that lbkd is left in no account — it only sees water and chambers, not who owns which book.
Treats subsumption (Q1/Q2) as a flow-coupling question (staircase vs flight) and can miss it entirely when the overlap is organizational rather than a serialization in the water path.
Assumes scarcity is the dominant constraint; if the real risk is correctness of scope boundaries or reconciliation rather than resource exhaustion, it over-weights budget/priming economics.
May treat the isolation crossover as purely an economic break-even and undervalue cases where shared-tree coordination is chosen for correctness reasons unrelated to water cost.
